question: What is the price tolerance for an invoice line where the unit price is higher than the PO?
gold: The excess on the line must be no more than the lower of 1% of the PO line value and ₹500.
answer_text:
Status: answered
Decision: Lower of 1% of the PO line value and ₹500 per line
Answer: A line priced above the PO passes only if the total excess on that line is no more than the lower of 1% of the PO line value and ₹500. [1] A line that fails is held with exception PRICE_VAR and sent to the buyer who raised the PO, who either amends the PO or asks the supplier for a credit note. [1] The PO buyer owns PRICE_VAR exceptions and must resolve them within 3 working days. [2] In practice, the note should state the line, item, invoice and PO rates, the excess amount and that it is above the ₹500 limit, rather than a bare 'price issue pls check'. [3]
Older sources (superseded): ₹1,000 (AP SOP v3.1); ₹1,000 (Part F); 2% (AP SOP v3.1); 2% (Part F)

question: Which GST return is used to decide whether input tax credit can be claimed?

question: How is a duplicate invoice detected?
gold: Same supplier GSTIN and normalised invoice number (spaces, slashes, hyphens, leading zeros and /A, /R or -REV suffixes removed), or same supplier, invoice date and total within ₹1.
answer_text:
Status: answered
Answer: A duplicate is detected by comparing each invoice, before indexing, against invoices received in the last 18 months for the same supplier using a normalised invoice number. [1] Normalisation removes spaces, slashes, hyphens and leading zeros and drops a trailing suffix of /A, /R or -REV. [1] Two invoices are a suspected duplicate when the supplier GSTIN and normalised number match, or when the supplier, invoice date and total amount (within ₹1) match. [1] Suspected duplicates go to the exception queue as DUP_SUSPECT and are never posted until a Senior Processor clears them, and if the system shows an amber flag you stop and raise DUP_SUSPECT without overriding. [1][2] In practice, the duplicate check is the first thing done before anything else, and when it flags amber you stop. [3]
Expert tip: Duplicate invoices must be sent to DUP_SUSPECT with a note and not overridden.
Older sources (superseded): reject the new invoice as a duplicate (AP SOP v3.1 §2); stop and raise DUP_SUSPECT; do not override (DI-03 Part A, step 2); stop_and_raise_DUP_SUSPECT (Video 1 [02:10])
